sensory.aromaNotes: Mild oyster aroma; less anise than some P. ostreatus strains
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Shelf-like pileus shreds into fibrous strips used in chicken-style analogs; widely cultivated oyster distinct from P. ostreatus.
sensory.preparationContext: Fresh clusters, sautéed or shredded; also dried
sensory.confidenceNotes: Meat-analog use inferred from Pleurotus cultivation and nutrition literature; species-specific sensory panels remain sparse.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: Pale cream to tan imbricate pilei with eccentric to lateral stipe and decurrent gills; typically smaller and paler than P. ostreatus

nutrition.preparationContext: Dry-weight proximate values aligned with Pleurotus nutrition reviews
nutrition.confidenceNotes: Uses Pleurotus-complex nutrition ranges; confirm against a species-specific proximate study before formulation.

geographic.habitat: Saprotroph on hardwood; warmer-weather oyster relative of P. ostreatus

strains.availabilityNotes: Add a verified culture-collection strain for Pleurotus pulmonarius.

commercialUse.applicationSummary: One of the most cultivated oyster mushrooms worldwide; sold fresh and used as shredded biomass in meat-analog and hybrid products.

companies.name: Commercial oyster farms (often labelled Indian / phoenix oyster)

productionProcess.title: Bag / block cultivation
productionProcess.description: Pasteurized straw, sawdust, or agricultural waste; fruits at warmer temperatures than many P. ostreatus strains.

commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Global cultivated crop; often marketed simply as oyster mushroom.

altProteinResearch.title: Growth and yield of Pleurotus species on agricultural wastes
altProteinResearch.summary: Documents scalable cultivation of Pleurotus, including pulmonarius-type oysters, on low-cost residues for protein biomass.
